messages:
Jordan S.: Quick kickoff thread for BrightFire POC — need to lock success criteria, integration checklist (SDK/auth/rate limits/streaming/retries), and timeline. Customer wants RAG search + semantic embeddings. POC target window: ~4 weeks.
Maria E.: Thanks — high level success criteria proposal: 1) Gen p95 latency <250ms at 512 tokens, 2) Search recall lift >=15% on their eval prompts, 3) End-to-end demo (ingest -> embeddings -> search -> RAG) with streaming responses in UI. Is that aligned?
Jordan S.: Yep, customer agreed to those targets in the call but wants confirmation on feasibility and estimated cost. Also they asked about auth and where logs live.
Vikram P.: Feasibility: Hosted API can meet those latencies with a small dedicated pool and prefix caching for RAG. Auth: standard Bearer API key (Authorization: Bearer <KEY>) for hosted. For Private/VPC we support KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys. Logs: request-level traces in Console with optional S3 export.
Maria E.: Integration notes for their engs: Node SDK example (streaming):
```
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-rlhf-7b', messages });
for await (const chunk of stream) { /* update UI */ }
```
And cURL quick auth example: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Vikram P.: Rate limits/quotas: default hosted limits are conservative (eg. 120 req/min). For POC we can provision a temporary bump: recommend 200 req/min and a token budget of 50M tokens for 4 weeks. If they need streaming concurrency >5 concurrent streams, we should use Dedicated.
Sam K.: Security checklist: they sent a short questionnaire this morning. Two flags: (1) need SOC2 attestation (we have it) and (2) they want data residency for logs — hosted can restrict region, Private gives full control. I asked them to mark which fields are deal-breakers.
Jordan S.: Pricing question from the buyer: how will POC be billed? They prefer a fixed POC estimate vs pay-as-you-go. Can we give a not-to-exceed quote for the 4-week run?
Maria E.: I'll draft a POC estimate: dedicated pool + rate bump + 50M token buffer + engineer support (5 days S/E time). Tentative figure and options: (A) usage-based with $X credit for the 4 weeks, (B) fixed POC fee with a one-time credit toward committed Dedicated.
Vikram P.: Implementation plan / timeline: Week 0: account + API keys + rate bump; Week 1: ingest connector + embeddings eval; Week 2: RAG integration + streaming UI; Week 3: tuning + evals; Week 4: final demo & handoff. Private/VPC adds ~2–3 weeks to spin up.
Maria E.: Retry guidance for their frontend: 429/500 -> exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries. For streaming, resume by reconnect and send last-K tokens of context if needed. Sample pseudo: `retryDelay = base * 2**attempt + random(0, jitter)`
Jordan S.: Customers also ask about rollbacks and fallback models — we can route to a smaller/cheaper model automatically if capacity constrained. Add that to the demo.
Sam K.: I'll own the security doc answers. Need the customer's infosec contact and the SG to sign off on data flows.
Maria E.: Action items: I will send Node SDK snippets, cost estimate, and a minimal prompt/eval suite they can run (10 queries across 3 use cases) by EOD tomorrow. Vikram: can you confirm the rate bump and token budget availability?
Vikram P.: Confirmed — we can do 200 rpm bump and reserve 50M tokens for the window. Tagging ops to provision once we have written approval.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: Dedicated-poc-46 pool reserved for brightfire-poc starting 2025-11-12 09:00 UTC.
Jordan S.: Great — I'll capture this in the SOW draft and loop legal for the POC fee. Next sync Tue 10am PT.
Maria E.: I'll prep the eval prompts (search relevance + hallucination checks) and share curl/sdk smoke tests.
Sam K.: I have the security answers skeleton; will complete after they confirm residency preference.
Jordan S.: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the single source for POC runbook.
